newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss life insurers oppose cabinet tax plan.
newsitem.headline: Swiss life insurers oppose cabinet tax plan.

text.p: The Swiss private life insurers' association VPL said it opposes a plan by the Swiss cabinet calling for a stamp tax on life insurance premiums.
VPL also did not rule out trying to block the tax plan with a citizens' vote if it passes parliament.
The cabinet's plan, announced on Wednesday as part of a package of stimulus measures, is expected to be discussed by parliament at the end of April.
It calls for a 2.5 percent stamp tax on life insurance premiums, aimed at compensating for declines in revenues expected from corporate tax reform.
VPL said it would consider whether or not to call for a referendum on the measure "in the interests of the insured" if parliament approved the measure.

VPL said the cabinet decision was not prudent given Swiss demographics. The aging population was likely to need more private old-age provisions in future due to strains expected on the federal pension provider AHV in the next century, it said.
